About.title: Specialists who speak your language
About.paragraph1: LegalWin is a Warsaw-based team of immigration, business and real-estate specialists working with clients from Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, Kazakhstan and the EU since 2019.
About.paragraph2: We handle cases at the Office for Foreigners, ZUS, tax authorities and KRS. Our clients are entrepreneurs, IT professionals, investors and families relocating to Poland.
About.point1: Transparent pricing - fixed fee per stage
About.point2: Dedicated case manager for every matter
About.point4: Service in Polish, Russian, Ukrainian and English

Cases.title: Real cases, real timelines
Cases.subtitle: We show it raw: what, how fast, and with what outcome. Names changed at clients' request.

items.title: IT specialist from Belarus
items.desc: Complete dossier on the first filing, no wezwania or follow-up requests. In Mazowieckie such cases often drag 8-14 months - here the decision came in about 4, thanks to a clean file and a by-the-book application.

items.title: Case stalled 14 months
items.desc: The client had waited over a year on a residence card with no movement. We filed a ponaglenie, then a delay complaint to the Administrative Court. The court ordered the voivode to decide and awarded compensation - the card issued ~9 weeks after the complaint.

items.title: Company set up from scratch
items.desc: Two founders from Kazakhstan. Via S24 the court entered the company into KRS in 2 business days; NIP and REGON were assigned automatically. The mBank account and VAT-R followed over the next ~3 weeks.

items.title: VAT for an EU contract
items.desc: The company needed active VAT and VAT-UE status for an EU client. We prepared the VAT-R and supporting notes - the tax office registered it without a clarification summons in about 3 weeks.

items.title: Senior developer from Belarus
items.desc: Salary above the EU Blue Card threshold. We assembled the contract, proof of qualifications and housing; in parallel we filed residence for the wife and child. Cards came in about 5 months.

items.title: PR by Polish origin
items.desc: Proof of Polish origin plus archival records. We obtained the missing certificates from civil registries in Poland and Ukraine. The voivode issued the permanent residence card in about 7 months.

items.title: Citizenship after PR
items.desc: Recognition as a Polish citizen: confirmed permanent residence, source of income, Polish at B1. The voivode issued a positive decision in about 8 months.

items.title: Reversing a residence denial
items.desc: The voivode refused, citing an unproven purpose of stay. We appealed to the Head of the Office for Foreigners with added evidence - the decision was reversed and the card issued.

items.title: Family reunification
items.desc: A residence-card holder bringing his family over. We prepared proof of housing, income and insurance for each member. All three cards issued in about 6 months.

items.title: Switching employer without losing status
items.desc: The client changed jobs mid single-permit. Within the statutory 15 days we filed the change-of-employer notice - he kept working legally while the new permit was processed separately.

items.title: Company struck off the VAT register
items.desc: The tax office removed the company from the VAT register for formal inactivity. We submitted explanations and proof of real activity - the active status was restored and contracts held.

items.title: Court overturns a PR denial
items.desc: The client was denied a permanent residence card on formal grounds. We went through the appeal, then a complaint to the Administrative Court - it quashed the denial and the card issued on reconsideration. Long, but won.

items.text: Set up our company in a week, with VAT and bank account. They reply on chat instantly, explain things clearly - no legalese soup.
items.author: Dmitry K.

items.text: Helped with an appeal after my PR denial. Second team I tried - and the only one who actually got it over the line.
items.author: Anna S.

items.text: Full package: airport pickup, apartment, PESEL, school for the kids, company set up. Cleared the whole Polish red-tape marathon in six weeks.
items.author: Sergey & Irina L.

items.text: Swapped my Ukrainian licence for a Polish one in 2 weeks. They told me exactly what to bring to starostwo so I didn't have to come back twice. Booked the medical exam in advance - I didn't have to hunt for a clinic.

items.text: Opened my JDG with the right PKD for freelance work, explained the health contribution and the 8.5% ryczałt rate. First invoice within a month, and a year in I'm comfortably on preferential ZUS.

items.author: Vitaly P.

items.text: Got my Karta Polaka and immediately moved on to citizenship by recognition. They prepared documents for both procedures at once - no translating and legalising the same papers twice.
items.author: Natalia K.

items.text: Bought a flat in Warsaw as a non-EU buyer - I needed MSWiA approval. They filed it together with due diligence on the property; three months later the permit was through. Without them I'd have lost the deposit.
items.author: Viktor Sh.

items.role: moved to Germany to join her husband

items.text: Got my Polish diploma apostilled for a job in Spain. They explained that it first needs certification and only then the apostille - I'd have definitely got the order wrong on my own. Documents arrived at my address in Valencia in 10 days, accepted with no issues.
items.author: Roman B.

items.author: Pavel G.

items.text: They handled an apostille on a power of attorney for a court case in Ukraine. Done properly, with translation, and they explained which wording was needed so the document would be accepted by the Ukrainian authority. Sent by DHL, arrived fast.
items.author: Svetlana M.

items.text: Exchanged my Belarusian licence for a Polish one. Belarus uses a different format, and LegalWin warned me in advance about an extra certificate and translation - so I cleared the starostwo on the first try, no repeat visits.
items.author: Andrey K.

items.text: They did get the licence exchanged in the end, everything sorted. But the badania lekarskie took longer than promised, and a couple of times I had to write myself to check the status. Happy with the result, just expected it faster.
items.author: Oleg R.

items.text: Did kod 95 via kwalifikacja przyspieszona - 140 hours. They helped me pick an OSK with a Russian-speaking instructor and booked the WORD exam without months of waiting. Five weeks later I was already hauling freight across the EU.
items.author: Denis F.

items.text: My kod 95 was up for renewal - szkolenie okresowe, 35 hours. They booked me onto a course near home, reminded me about deadlines, and I got the new card on time with no downtime at work.
items.author: Maksim Z.

items.text: Ordered sworn translations of a document package for ZUS - certificates, work record, statements. Done in two days, and the tłumacz przysięgły stamp was accepted at the urząd without a single question.
items.author: Yulia N.

items.text: They translated the company's founding documents from English to Polish to open a bank account. The translation was precise, legal terms in place - the bank opened the account with no corrections needed.
items.author: Artem V.

items.text: Needed sworn translations of medical documents for treatment abroad. Done neatly and fast, and they helped me work out exactly which papers the clinic required. Very attentive throughout.
items.author: Lyudmila P.

items.text: I came to them about a residence card. I did get the card in the end and the work was done. But communication was lacking - sometimes several days with no reply, I had to chase and ask for status myself. Happy with the outcome, but the waiting frayed my nerves.
items.author: Oksana T.

items.text: They apostilled a marriage certificate and sent it to Italy for family reunification. Done with a sworn Italian translation, all correct - the consulate accepted the package straight away.
items.author: Tatiana S.

items.text: Needed a sworn translation of a court ruling for Ukraine. Translated correctly with the right legal terminology, certified and sent. The document was accepted by the Ukrainian authority with no questions.
items.author: Veronika L.

items.text: I applied for a residence card through work with three weeks left on my visa. They put the file together fast, filed it at the Mazowiecki Urząd Wojewódzki in time, and I got the stamp in my passport the same day. The decision came seven months later - a card for three years.
items.author: Ruslan A.

items.text: I changed employers in the middle of my residence card procedure. I was sure I'd have to start over - turned out I only had to notify the urząd and file a new załącznik nr 1. They explained it in ten minutes and sent the papers the same day.
items.author: Alina Z.

items.text: I was renewing my residence card, the old one expired in March. They reminded me well ahead that the application has to go in before it runs out, otherwise you lose legal stay. The only thing: the filing queue at the urząd was booked a month out, but they warned me about that upfront.
items.author: Taras M.

items.text: I needed a criminal record certificate for a new employer in Norway. They handled it through e-KRK under a power of attorney, with the apostille and a sworn English translation right away. Done in four days, and I never had to travel to Warsaw.
items.author: Bohdan S.

items.text: I was gathering documents for citizenship and needed criminal record certificates from the KRK and from Ukraine. They pointed out that the Polish one is only accepted while it's recent, and worked out when to order it so it wouldn't expire before filing. A small thing, but without it the whole file would have come back.
items.author: Iryna V.

items.text: I needed an apostille on the KRS extract and the company's articles to open a bank account in the UAE. They had it notarised, got the apostille at the MSZ and did a sworn English translation. The bank accepted the whole package without a single comment.
items.author: Stanislav E.

items.text: Your first weeks in Poland are PESEL, meldunek and profil zaufany - without them you can't open an account or book a doctor. They made the appointment, came with me and closed all three in one visit. Six months later I came back to them for my residence card.
items.author: Daria F.

Faq.title: Frequently asked

items.q: How much is the first consultation?
items.a: The first consultation is free. We review your situation, tell you which documents you actually need, and lay out timing and cost before you pay anything. If deep document review or a written opinion is required, follow-up sessions start at 200 PLN depending on complexity.

items.q: How long does a residence permit take?
items.a: On average 6–8 months. The statutory deadline for the wojewoda (regional governor) is 90 days, but in Mazowieckie Voivodeship in 2026 decisions realistically take 6–14 months. A full document pack and a clean MOS v2.0 filing keep you closer to the lower bound. If it drags, we file a ponaglenie (motion to expedite) and, if needed, a skarga na bezczynność (complaint of inaction) to the Voivodeship Administrative Court.

items.q: Is a residence permit the same as a work permit?
items.a: No — they are separate. A residence permit lets you stay; to work you generally also need a basis such as an oświadczenie (employer's declaration) or a zezwolenie na pracę (work permit). We check your situation and arrange the right one alongside your stay.

items.q: Do I qualify for the EU Blue Card?
items.a: If you have higher qualifications (a degree or equivalent experience) and a job offer paying at least 150% of the national average — about 160,264 PLN gross a year for 2026 applications. The permit runs up to 3 years, the state fee is 440 PLN, and after 12 months you gain EU mobility. We assess eligibility and file through the MOS portal.

items.q: Can I exchange my non-EU driving licence for a Polish one?
items.a: Yes. You will need a sworn translation (tłumacz przysięgły), an application at the wydział komunikacji (traffic department) and the fee (100.50 PLN); licences from non–Vienna-Convention countries also need a medical certificate. Total cost is usually 180–300 PLN. Once you have lived here over 185 days a year, the exchange is required — we handle the paperwork end to end.

items.q: What's included in the price and how does payment work?
items.a: Our fee and the government charges (opłata skarbowa) are separate amounts — we always show them apart, with no hidden add-ons. For most cases payment is staged: part at the start, part at key milestones. After the first consultation you receive a fixed quote tailored to your case.

items.q: What should I do if I'm denied?
items.a: We analyse the grounds for refusal (decyzja odmowna) and file an appeal (odwołanie) within 14 days — the statutory window. We have successful appeals on TRC, permanent residence, citizenship and international protection, including through the Voivodeship Administrative Court. Even when the clock is tight, show us the decision first.

items.q: Do you work remotely and with other cities?
items.a: Yes. Clients from other Polish cities and from abroad run their cases entirely online: notarial power of attorney, a direct line to your case manager and a client portal with live statuses. A visit to our office at ul. Świętokrzyska 30 in Warsaw is not required.

items.q: What languages do you work in?
items.a: Polish, Russian, Ukrainian, English. All documents come translated into your language, and we produce sworn translations (tłumaczenia przysięgłe) ready for filing with the urząd.
